Today's big story

PMI beat, Iran wobble — Nasdaq 13-day streak snaps.

Flash PMIs cleared the bar: Composite 52.0 (3-month high), Manufacturing 54.0, Services 51.3 — enough to keep a "hold and watch" FOMC alive. But the risk rally reversed by midday on fresh Iran war headlines. Nasdaq closed −0.89% at 24,438.50, snapping its 13-day winning streak. S&P 7,108.40, Dow 49,310.32, Russell −0.86%. BTC held near $77.8K on the reversal; oil spiked on the geopolitics. UMich sentiment final + New Home Sales land at 10 ET today, then it's all eyes on the Apr 28–29 FOMC.

01 — Fintech pulse

Flash PMI clears the bar — but the Fed still isn't the story.


April's Flash US Composite PMI printed 52.0, a 3-month high, with manufacturing at 54.0 and services at 51.3. Both came in above consensus and locked in a "hold and watch" FOMC narrative for next week. Market pricing shifted: the June cut odds that were heating up on March data went back to coin-flip. But the macro is no longer where the alpha is.

The trade is structural: tokenized Treasuries $12B+, stablecoin supply at all-time highs, CFTC-regulated perps live, tokenized equities spreading to more venues every week. The Fed moves rates by quarter-points; the on-chain financial system is moving the plumbing by orders of magnitude. When PMI prints become noise because your portfolio lives across four surfaces 24/7, you're early. Most retail isn't.
